Path Traversal: 'dir/../../filename' in moment.locale
advisory.description:
### Impact
This vulnerability impacts npm (server) users of moment.js, especially if user provided locale string, eg `fr` is directly used to switch moment locale.

### Patches
This problem is patched in 2.29.2, and the patch can be applied to all affected versions (from 1.0.1 up until 2.29.1, inclusive).

### Workarounds
Sanitize user-provided locale name before passing it to moment.js.

advisory.summary: Prototype Pollution in lodash
advisory.description:
Versions of lodash prior to 4.17.19 are vulnerable to Prototype Pollution. The functions `pick`, `set`, `setWith`, `update`, `updateWith`, and `zipObjectDeep` allow a malicious user to modify the prototype of Object if the property identifiers are user-supplied. Being affected by this issue requires manipulating objects based on user-provided property values or arrays.

This vulnerability causes the addition or modification of an existing property that will exist on all objects and may lead to Denial of Service or Code Execution under specific circumstances.

advisory.summary: jsonwebtoken's insecure implementation of key retrieval function could lead to Forgeable Public/Private Tokens from RSA to HMAC
advisory.description:
# Overview

Versions `<=8.5.1` of `jsonwebtoken` library can be misconfigured so that passing a poorly implemented key retrieval function (referring to the `secretOrPublicKey` argument from the [readme link](https://github.com/auth0/node-jsonwebtoken#jwtverifytoken-secretorpublickey-options-callback)) will result in incorrect verification of tokens. There is a possibility of using a different algorithm and key combination in verification  than the one that was used to sign the tokens. Specifically, tokens signed with an asymmetric public key could be verified with a symmetric HS256 algorithm. This can lead to successful validation of forged tokens. 

# Am I affected?

You will be affected if your application is supporting usage of both symmetric key and asymmetric key in jwt.verify() implementation with the same key retrieval function. 

# How do I fix it?
 
Update to version 9.0.0.

# Will the fix impact my users?

There is no impact for end users

advisory.summary: Multer Denial of Service via Crafted Multipart Field Names
advisory.description: multer versions >= 1.4.4-lts.1 and < 2.3.0 are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). A crafted multipart upload request with specially constructed field names causes the multipart parser to throw an uncaught exception, crashing the Node.js process. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this to terminate the server. Fixed in 2.3.0.

advisory.summary: multer Denial of Service via Oversized Array Index in Field Names
advisory.description: multer versions >= 1.4.4-lts.1 and < 2.3.0 are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS). When a multipart field name contains an oversized array index (e.g., `field[999999999]`), the parser performs an allocation proportional to the index value, exhausting available memory. Unauthenticated attackers can trigger an out-of-memory crash via a single malformed request. Fixed in 2.3.0.

advisory.summary: multer File Descriptor Leak on Aborted Uploads (DoS)
advisory.description: multer version 2.2.0 using diskStorage fails to close the destination write stream when a multipart upload is aborted prematurely. Each aborted upload leaks an open file descriptor and retains disk blocks until process termination. Repeated aborted upload requests exhaust the process's file descriptor limit, making the service unavailable. Fixed in 2.3.0. CVE-2026-77037.

advisory.summary: nodemailer ReDoS via Quadratic Complexity in addressparser
advisory.description: nodemailer versions < 9.1.0 contain a Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerability in the bundled addressparser module. The email address parsing regex exhibits quadratic time complexity on inputs that contain many separators or nested comment constructs. A single crafted recipient address can block the Node.js event loop for seconds. Fixed in 9.1.0. CVE-2026 (CWE-400/407).

advisory.summary: nodemailer IDN/Punycode Normalization Bypass Allows Domain Allow-List Evasion
advisory.description: nodemailer versions < 9.1.0 use a bundled RFC-3492 Punycode codec without UTS-46 normalization. International domain names containing invisible Unicode characters (e.g., U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN) are encoded differently from standards-compliant parsers, allowing a crafted recipient domain to pass allow-list validation while actually resolving to a different registrable domain. Fixed in 9.1.0.

advisory.summary: nodemailer RFC 5322 Comment Parsing Allows Mail Redirection to Attacker Domain
advisory.description: nodemailer versions >= 6.9.16 and < 9.1.0 mishandle RFC 5322 comments within email domain parts. A comment such as `(x)` between domain segments is concatenated rather than discarded, so an address like `user@good-corp.com(x)evil.com` resolves to `good-corp.comevil.com`, enabling mail redirection to an attacker-controlled domain. Fixed in 9.1.0.

advisory.summary: js-yaml Denial of Service via Unbounded YAML Merge Key Expansion
advisory.description: js-yaml versions >= 4.0.0 and < 4.3.2 (and >= 3.0.0 and < 3.15.2 on the 3.x branch) do not enforce a limit on the total number of merge keys (`<<`) resolved during YAML parsing. A crafted YAML document using many empty merge sources can exhaust CPU and memory proportional to the count of merge keys. Fixed in 4.3.2 (and 3.15.2 for the 3.x branch) by introducing a `maxTotalMergeKeys` cap.

advisory.summary: morgan Log Forging via Unicode Line Separators in HTTP Request Fields
advisory.description: morgan versions < 1.12.0 do not sanitize Unicode line terminators (U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) from logged HTTP request fields such as User-Agent and URL. An attacker can inject these characters to forge additional log lines, making malicious activity appear legitimate or hiding real events. Fixed in 1.12.0, which strips U+2028 and U+2029 from all logged values. CWE-117.

advisory.summary: smol-toml Infinite Loop Denial of Service via Malformed TOML Input
advisory.description: smol-toml versions <= 1.7.0 enter an infinite loop when the parse() function processes a TOML document containing an array or inline table whose last value is followed by a comment with no trailing newline. The parser resets to the document start on each iteration, consuming 100% CPU indefinitely. Fixed in 1.7.1 with proper loop termination. CVE-2026-85730.

nodes.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')

advisory.summary: sharp Heap Buffer Overflow via Malicious AVIF Image (libheif)
advisory.description: sharp versions < 0.35.4 bundle a vulnerable version of libheif that contains heap buffer overflow flaws (CWE-122) when decoding attacker-crafted AVIF image data. On glibc-based Linux systems, processing an untrusted AVIF file can lead to remote code execution with the application's privileges. Fixed in sharp 0.35.4, which upgrades the bundled libheif to 1.23.2.

advisory.summary: hono Path Traversal in toSSG() Allows File Writes Outside Output Directory
advisory.description: hono versions < 4.13.5 contain an incomplete remediation for a prior path traversal in the toSSG() static site generation function. The path normalization routine fails to collapse consecutive parent-directory segments, allowing route parameters with repeated `..` sequences to bypass directory boundary checks and write files outside the designated output directory. Fixed in 4.13.5. CVE-2026-84365.

nodes.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

advisory.summary: hono parseBody() Memory Exhaustion via Deeply Nested Dot-Notation Fields
advisory.description: hono versions < 4.13.5 do not limit nesting depth when parseBody() converts dot-notation form field names into nested objects. Attackers can craft requests where a single field name with deep dot-notation (e.g., `a.b.c...x`) triggers heap allocations far exceeding the request body size. Concurrent malicious requests can exhaust available memory and crash the server. Only affects applications that explicitly enable dot-notation parsing. Fixed in 4.13.5. CVE-2026-84364.

advisory.summary: astro Remote Code Execution via Malicious AVIF Image in Default Sharp Image Service
advisory.description: astro versions < 7.2.8 use the default Sharp image service, which bundles a vulnerable libheif containing out-of-bounds read and write flaws (CWE-125, CWE-787). A malicious AVIF image submitted for optimization can trigger these memory safety violations and achieve remote code execution with no authentication or user interaction required. CVSS 9.8. Fixed in astro 7.2.8.

advisory.summary: @tiptap/core ReDoS in Markdown Attribute Parsers
advisory.description: @tiptap/core versions >= 3.7.0 and < 3.30.5 contain two quadratic Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) vulnerabilities in the default Markdown attribute parsers. The first is in block attribute parsing via an unanchored greedy expression that rescans repeated prefixes; the second is in inline shortcode attribute parsing via an unanchored greedy key expression. A small crafted Markdown input can freeze the Node.js event loop. Affected functions: createAtomBlockMarkdownSpec, createBlockMarkdownSpec, createInlineMarkdownSpec. Fixed in 3.30.5.

advisory.summary: omniroute Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via ACP Custom-Agent Endpoint
advisory.description: omniroute versions <= 3.8.50 expose a POST /api/acp/agents endpoint that accepts user-controlled binary and versionCommand parameters without sufficient validation. The application immediately executes the supplied versionCommand via execFileSync() after saving the agent. When requireLogin=false, this endpoint is reachable without authentication, allowing arbitrary Node.js code and OS command execution. No patch is currently available. CVE-2026-88062.
